newsitem.title: FRANCE: French unions fear job losses at utilities -paper.
newsitem.headline: French unions fear job losses at utilities -paper.

text.p: The French CGT and CFDT trade unions fear up to 10,000 jobs could be lost over the next five years at the EdF and GdF state-owned electricity and gas utilities.

The Journal de Dimanche Sunday newspaper reported that the unions at Electricite de France and Gaz de France received a working paper from the management which "gave a range of employment outlooks, depending on development, competitiveness and organisation of working time.
"In the most pessimistic hypothesis, 14,400 jobs could be destroyed between now and 2001, with 4,320 being created," the newspaper reported.
The most favourable outlook was for 9,000 jobs to go and 7,360 new posts to be created, with a net loss of 1,640, it said. Talks are due to open on Monday, it added.

The French government suffers from low standings in public opinion polls, weakened by a record unemployment rate of 12.6 percent. Unions have been demonstrating this weekend to mark the anniversary of last year's protests against social security reforms aimed at cutting the state deficit.
